This is a presentation difference that preserves the exact key wording the user needs. (2) The agent included quotes and numbering; that does not change the content.

Critical issues: None. The DOM evidence confirms the agent was on https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/UNRATE with the header "Unemployment Rate (UNRATE)". The metadata shown in the DOM includes "Units: Percent , Seasonally Adjusted" and "Frequency: Monthly", matching the agent’s reported Units=Percent, Frequency=Monthly, and Seasonal adjustment=Seasonally Adjusted. The latest three displayed observations in the DOM table are explicitly "Aug 2026: 4.1", "Jul 2026: 4.1", and "Jun 2026: 4.2" in that order, matching the agent’s output exactly for month/year and values. Constraint compliance is also supported: DOM shows the user is not signed in and there is no subscribe/account creation action; the agent stopped after recording the requested metadata and three observations. Overall, the agent delivered the correct series metadata and the correct three latest displayed observations from the UNRATE page, satisfying the task as an average user would expect.
outcome.primary_intent: The user wanted the agent to open the FRED UNRATE (Unemployment Rate) series page and accurately transcribe (1) the series metadata—units, frequency, and seasonal-adjustment status—and (2) the three latest observation months and values shown on that same UNRATE page. A reasonable user would not be flexible on using the wrong series, wrong months/values, or paraphrasing/altering the exact displayed wording/decimals; they would be flexible on minor formatting like whether seasonal adjustment is listed on its own line vs. noted as part of the units line.
